title: Eligibility Screen setup
intro: This wizard installs your own copy of the Eligibility Screen. The Eligibility Screen is a web page for families of student athletes. A parent enters a name, an email, a division target (DI or DII), the number of core courses done, the core GPA and the graduation year. The page applies fixed NCAA initial-eligibility rules. It shows an On Track, At Risk or Off Track read with flags and next steps. Each run saves a lead in your database. It emails the parent a link to a result card. It also emails you. The code comes from the repository keyona-rerev/eligibility-screen. It has two pages and two Netlify functions. It runs on your own GitHub, Supabase, Netlify, Cloudflare and Resend accounts. The result is a risk screen only. It is not an official ruling. The NCAA Eligibility Center makes the official decision. You need about 45 minutes.

steps.title: Check what you need
steps.instructions:
Open these free accounts. Sign in to each one.

- GitHub (to hold your copy of the code)
- Supabase (the database for leads and result cards)
- Netlify (to host the pages and the two functions)
- Cloudflare (for the Turnstile spam check)
- Resend (to send emails). This one is optional.
- Anthropic (for an API key). This one is optional. Without it, the page uses fixed plain-language text.

Enter the name of your business or program. Enter your GitHub username.
steps.checkbox_label: I am signed in to my accounts.
steps.verify_hint: You can open github.com, supabase.com, netlify.com and dash.cloudflare.com as {{github_username}} or as your business {{business_name}}.

steps.title: Copy the code to your GitHub
steps.instructions:
Open the repository keyona-rerev/eligibility-screen on GitHub. Click Fork. Choose your own account. Choose the repository name below. Do not rename the files.

If you cannot fork, ask ReRev Labs for a copy.
steps.checkbox_label: My copy of the repository exists.
steps.verify_hint: Open https://github.com/{{github_username}}/{{repo_name}}. You see index.html, report.html, supabase.sql and a netlify folder.

steps.title: Create the database table
steps.instructions:
Create a new project in Supabase, or pick one you already own. Enter its project reference below.

Open the SQL Editor in Supabase. Paste the SQL below. Click Run. This makes one table for leads and result cards. The table is private. Only your server code can read it.

This step never needs a key in this wizard. You will put the Supabase service key in Netlify later.

copy.label: SQL to run in the Supabase SQL Editor

steps.checkbox_label: The SQL ran without an error.
steps.verify_hint: In Table Editor, you see the table eligibility_reports. It has the columns full_name, email, division, core_done, core_gpa, grad_year, verdict, report, ip and token.

steps.title: Create your Netlify site
steps.instructions:
Open Netlify. Click Add new project, then Import an existing project. Choose GitHub. Pick your repository {{repo_name}}. Do not change the build settings. The file netlify.toml sets them. Choose your site name below. Click Deploy.

The first deploy works but the tool will not run yet. You add the settings in the next steps.
steps.verify_hint: Open {{app_url}}. You see the eligibility form.

steps.title: Create the Turnstile spam check
steps.instructions:
Open the Cloudflare dashboard. Go to Turnstile. Click Add widget. Give it any name. Add the hostname below. Choose the Managed mode. Click Create.

Cloudflare shows a site key and a secret key. Copy the site key into the field below. The site key is public. Keep the secret key private. You paste the secret key only in Netlify, in a later step.
steps.checkbox_label: The Turnstile widget exists and I saved the secret key in a safe place.
steps.verify_hint: In Cloudflare, Turnstile lists a widget with the hostname {{netlify_site_name}}.netlify.app.

steps.title: Set up email (optional)
steps.instructions:
Skip this step if you do not want emails. The tool still saves each lead and shows the result card.

Open Resend. Add and verify your sending domain. Create an API key. Do not paste the key here. You paste it in Netlify later.

Enter the sender address and the address that gets lead alerts. Use the same domain you verified.
steps.checkbox_label: I finished the email setup or I chose to skip it.
steps.verify_hint: Resend shows your domain as Verified. You chose the sender {{from_email}} and the alert address {{notify_email}}, or you skipped both.

steps.title: Add your brand and the Turnstile site key
steps.instructions:
Open your repository {{repo_name}} on GitHub. Edit the file index.html.

1. Find the text YOUR_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY. Replace it with the site key from the Turnstile step.
2. Replace the brand name Athlete Site with {{business_name}}. Also replace the link to athlete-site.com with your own link. The brand appears in the page title, the card header, the call-to-action box and the footer.
3. Open report.html. Make the same brand changes.
4. Open netlify/functions/eligibility.js. Replace the brand text Athlete Site in the parent email and in the lead alert subject.

Commit each change to the main branch.

copy.label: The line to find in index.html
The same line with your site key

steps.checkbox_label: I saved my changes in GitHub.
steps.verify_hint: In index.html, the text YOUR_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY is gone. The line shows {{turnstile_site_id}}.

steps.title: Add the settings in Netlify
steps.instructions:
Open your site {{netlify_site_name}} in Netlify. Go to Site configuration, then Environment variables. Add each variable below.

Paste your own values in place of the placeholders. The Supabase service key is on the API page of your Supabase project. Use the service role key, not the anon key. Never put any key in GitHub, in the page or in this wizard.

The variables EMAIL_FROM, EMAIL_REPLY_TO and LEAD_NOTIFY_TO have a built-in fallback address that belongs to ReRev Labs. Always set them if you use email.

The variables ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, RESEND_API_KEY and the three email variables are optional.
steps.checkbox_label: I added all the variables in Netlify.
steps.verify_hint: Netlify lists SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY, TURNSTILE_SECRET and DAILY_CAP. It lists the optional ones you chose.

steps.title: Deploy again
steps.instructions:
In Netlify, open Deploys. Click Trigger deploy, then Deploy site. Wait until the status is Published.

The code reads the settings only at deploy time and run time. A new deploy makes sure it uses your page edits and your settings.
steps.verify_hint: Open {{app_url}}. The Turnstile box appears above the Run button. Your brand name shows on the page.

steps.title: Run a first test
steps.instructions:
Open {{app_url}}. Enter a test name and your own email. Pick Division I. Enter 9 core courses, a core GPA of 3.1 and a graduation year two to three years from now. Complete the Turnstile check. Click Run the screen.

You see a result card with a risk read. Click the link to view and download the card. If you set up email, check your inbox for the parent email and the lead alert.
steps.checkbox_label: The result card, the saved lead and the emails work.
steps.verify_hint: The card shows On Track, At Risk or Off Track. In Supabase, the table eligibility_reports has one new row. If the page shows 'not fully configured', check SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY in Netlify. If the check says it cannot verify you, check the Turnstile site key and the hostname {{netlify_site_name}}.netlify.app.

steps.title: Learn how to update
steps.instructions:
ReRev Labs publishes a version history for this product. Open the history page that came with this wizard. Compare the newest version with your own version. Your version is the date of the newest commit that you copied from keyona-rerev/eligibility-screen.

To update, open your repository {{repo_name}} on GitHub. Click Sync fork. Netlify then deploys the new code. Check the history page for extra steps, for example a database change. Your own edits of the brand text can cause a merge conflict. Keep a note of your edits.
steps.checkbox_label: I know where the version history is and how to sync my copy.
steps.verify_hint: You can open the history page and find your version.
